headline: Board reviews tobacco retailer compliance and plans regulation amendment; approved July 9 minutes 4-0
summary: The Board discussed enforcement efforts against tobacco retailers selling non-FDA-approved products, including legal pushback from one retailer's lawyer and a response from the Attorney General's office. Staff gave updates on septic compliance, food safety, opioid abatement, a state performance survey, prevention programs, and communicable disease trends. The Board agreed to wait until September to act on a proposed regulation amendment requiring retailer compliance with federal, state, and local law.
decisions: Approved the July 9, 2026 Board of Health minutes as amended, 4-0.

plain_text:
CITY OF GLOUCESTER 
Board of Health 
Minutes of the Meeting 
August 6, 2026, 5:30 p.m. 
Harbormaster Conference Room & 
Hybrid Meeting Via Zoom 
 
Board members present: Chairperson: Joseph Rosa; Vice-Chairperson: Dr. Eric Kaplan; Jesse 
Dole; and Thomas Markert. Absent: Erin George.  
 
Also present: Health Director: Dominique Hurley; Regional Prevention Director: Chelsea 
Goldstein-Walsh; Assistant Health Director: Gabrielle White; Public Health Excellence Program 
Manager: Danielle Larabee; Public Health Nurse: Cindy Juncker; Administrative Assistant: 
Alison Battle. 
 
The meeting started at 5:30 p.m.  
 
Public Oral Communication 
  
There was no “Public Oral Communication”.  
 
Approval of Minutes 
                  
MOTION by Dr. Kaplan to approve the Gloucester Board of Health minutes of the meeting of 
July 9 th, 2026 as amended. Seconded by Mr. Dole. Carried 4-0.  
 
Nicotine and Tobacco Retailer Report  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that a letter went out in early June to tobacco retailers reminding them that if 
they have products that are not FDA approved, they can't sell them. She stated that the FDA 
has a product database that retailers can use to confirm if they can sell a product or not. She 
stated that at the last Board of Health meeting the Board asked the Health Department to ask 
retailers to provide an inventory list of all the nicotine and tobacco products currently being sold 
that do not have an FDA marketing order. She stated that of the 29 retailers that were contacted 
12 responded and those that responded were adamant that they were not carrying any of the 
products on their shelves with the exception of 3 retailers all with the same owner. She stated 
that they have documents from their manufacturers in China, one being an acceptance of the 
application to the FDA for consideration (but not with any sort of approval) however there is an 
approval letter that is cut by the manufacturer. She stated that they visited three of the retailers 
that did not respond, including one owned by Sunny Patel, who attended the July Board of 
Health meeting, and they had several products out that are not allowed to be sold and products 
on the counter (which is a violation of State law). She stated that Mr. Patel’s lawyer contacted 
the Health Department and told them to stop all enforcement or risk being added to a pending
Page 2 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
August 6, 2026 
 
lawsuit. She stated that the Attorney General’s office responded saying they could add them to 
the lawsuit if they wish and added the following: 
● “First, to the extent that paragraph 2 on page 2 of your letter implies that DPH has 
advised non-defendant municipalities to proceed with imposing fines or permit 
suspensions, that is not the case.  DPH has not offered any such guidance to non-
defendants.  If asked, DPH would advise non-defendants to consult their own counsel.  I 
hope this clarifies things for you.  
● Second, it is DPH’s position that the motion and briefing schedule submitted to the Court 
bind the parties, but do not bind non-parties.  So far as I know, the parties have honored 
the agreement on both sides.  But for the avoidance of doubt, we do not see it as binding 
on the 336 other cities and towns in the Commonwealth that are not defendants in this 
case.  
● Third, recall that the defendants to the litigation agree not to take action against the 
permits of plaintiffs or similarly situated business or to impose any fines arising out of the 
issues identified in the Enforcement Notices.  That does not, in DPH’s view, extend to 
other regulatory activity such as conducting inspections or sending additional notices of 
potential future enforcement.  I just want to make sure we’re clear on this, because in the 
event that defendants prevail on the PI motion, the municipalities will want these 
products off the shelves and will expect retailers to move quickly.  I think it’s only fair to 
your clients and other similarly situated businesses that they have reasonable notice of 
the defendants’ position, even while they are not at immediate risk of enforcement 
pursuant to our agreement.”     
 
Ms. Hurley suggested that the Board consider updating their local regulations to more explicitly 
require that retailers comply with federal, state, and local law. She suggested that they amend 
the regulation to require that the retailer demonstrate attention to federal law as part of their 
application process and they could accomplish this by having the retailer submit inventory 
reports with documentation and attestation showing how they are compliant to federal, state, 
and local law, with that inventory list. The board discussed amending the regulation to explicitly 
condition it upon compliance with state, local, and federal law. 
 
Ms. Hurley commended the 12 of our 29 retailers that did exactly the right thing and were quite 
clear in their willingness and the actions that they took. She stated that she has had a few calls 
from retailers complaining that they have done the right thing and other retailers aren't doing the 
right thing and they're losing sales to other retailers because of that. Chairperson Rosa 
suggested that they put something together that those retailers could post in their windows that 
says that they're in full compliance with the rules and regulations of Gloucester. The Board also 
discussed putting something in the newspaper. Ms. Hurley suggested that the Board wait until 
September to take any action. She stated that she will have a draft amendment to the regulation 
for the Board to review at the September meeting.  
 
 
 
Health Director’s Recap
Page 3 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
August 6, 2026 
 
Presented by Dominique Hurley 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that one of the Health Department’s goals is that they have to improve on 
compliance to local and state regulations through educational outreach. She stated that they're 
continuing with their septic compliance campaigns of 709 properties in Ward 5 that have no 
record of a pump out in three and a half years. She stated that they had 175 properties in Wards 
1 through 4 that were outstanding and non-compliant and 149 of them are now in compliance 
and of the 26 remaining, 21 are inactive.  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that the Health Department is conducting active managerial control food 
trainings, distributing temporary food and vendor information packets, and performing courtesy 
walkthroughs in collaboration with the Building Department. She stated that their food inspector, 
Ms. Vorias, is actively educating food operators on legal requirements.  
 
Ms. Hurley commended Mr. Williamson and Ms. Vorias for their work on these campaigns, not 
only in helping people understand the requirements but also for building relationships.  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that the next goal was to increase compliance with state sanitary code. She 
stated that they've isolated a lot of the other things that the Housing Inspector, Ms. Turko was 
doing so that she can really focus on housing. She stated that the rental registry has an entirely 
new approach where they are focused on education of the law, not necessarily the inspection, 
with the thought that the Building Department would be doing the inspections.  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that their third goal was continuous quality improvement through public health 
excellence. She stated that they have been digitizing several different types of files and they're 
at the end stages of getting that work done and in the beginning stages of QAQC on the quality 
of it, and making it available to the public. 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that the fourth goal that has yet to be completed is advancing opioid 
abatement and efforts by driving down internal costs and improving deployment operations. She 
stated that Carla Dellaporta is the program manager and is making some good progress on 
improving those operations. She stated that the mayor recently made the decision to fund three 
more community organizations that are focusing on prevention and harm reduction for opioid 
use disorder. She stated that they are working on getting agreements in place, to support that 
fund deployment right now. 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that the last goal was to fill two open Board of Health seats, which they have 
done. She stated that they are in the process of giving the Mayor's office an update on all of the 
goals.  
 
 
 
 
 
SAPHE 2.0 Performance Standards Survey Results
Page 4 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
August 6, 2026 
 
 
Ms. Larabee gave Board members results that provided an overview of Gloucester's results 
from the Massachusetts Department of Public Health Office of Local & Regional Health 
Performance Standards Survey. She stated that the overview shows where the Health 
Department is meeting state expectations, identifies areas that need improvement, explains the 
reasons for any gaps, and outlines the steps planned in FY27 to address those gaps. She 
reviewed items in the survey that covered various aspects including foundational public health 
services, permits, complaints, and environmental health establishments, with responses ranging 
from limited to comprehensive on many questions. She stated that the State will use the survey 
results to make recommendations for future funding, grant opportunities, and training in the fall, 
marking the first year of this required statewide assessment process. Ms. Hurley stated that the 
Health Department conducted a similar self-assessment survey for the last two years with 
questions, not as detailed, but this is the first year that it is a statewide common survey for all as 
a requirement. Ms. Larabee stated that this survey will be required every year moving forward.  
 
Public Health Excellence (PHE) Grant Reporting 
 
Ms. Larabee gave Board members a brief overview of the projects that she is managing with 
Gloucester and Manchester under the Public Health Excellence Grant. She stated that one 
project is file digitization with the hope to eventually have a public portal, where people can go in 
and pull their septic records, hazardous waste records, well records, and then in the future, 
potentially more. She stated that another project is the septic compliance software on which Mr. 
Williamson and Mr. Smith have been working really hard. She stated that this allows all of the 
pumpers and haulers to submit their O&M reports and pump reports in the field. She stated that 
the third project involves Berger Food Safety Consulting, which started two weeks ago to help 
with the summer surge of food inspections, with weekly reports being provided and Ms. Vorias 
handling reinspections. She reviewed a strategic assessment project led by Aldrich Tobin 
Partners focusing on health and human services needs in both Manchester and Gloucester, 
with data collection underway and recommendations expected in early fall.  
 
 
Prevention Team Reporting 
Presented by Chelsea Goldstein-Walsh 
 
Ms. Goldstein-Walsh stated that they are waiting for the final data report from the Risk Behavior 
Survey. She stated that she does not yet have permission to share the data in a public forum.  
 
Ms. Goldstein-Walsh stated that with the new school year starting, they have really been 
focusing heavily on recruitment. She stated that they have a cohort of students who are 
transitioning to high school, and will be joining their high school group and they've spent the last 
couple of weeks visiting the O'Maley Academy Move Up Camp for incoming 6th graders, to 
orient them to the Gloucester Youth Leadership Council and share what they do. She stated 
that they also have an open house scheduled for later this month on August 27th, at Cape Ann 
Lanes from 4 to 6.30. She stated that it's a free bowling event with free food, and it's open to all.

Minutes of the Board of Health 
August 6, 2026 
 
 
Ms. Goldstein-Walsh stated that they have been holding planning meetings for their parent 
program that will be launching in the fall. She stated that the program is funded by their 
Prevention and Early Childhood Grant, focused on the transitional age from elementary to 
middle school, supporting both youth and their caregivers. She stated that they will be offering a 
free 6-week parent cohort program for parents of that transitional age, parents and caregivers of 
transitional age into middle school. 
 
Ms. Goldstein-Walsh stated that another parent-focused effort that they are planning right is 
educational outreach to parents and caregivers on how to have those conversations with their 
young people, with their teens and their kids around challenging topics, such as mental health, 
substance use, digital safety, and just trying to provide information using evidence-based 
resources to make sure that parents feel equipped and confident on how to have these 
conversations and where to find accurate information.  
 
Ms. Goldstein-Walsh stated that Action, Inc. will be managing the financial management of 
recovery housing for the RIZE Mosaic OAC grant and they submitted their Year 2 progress 
report on July 31st.  
 
Communicable Disease Reporting 
 
Ms. Juncker reported that in Massachusetts there have been 147 Cyclospora cases reported 
and less than five in Gloucester.  
 
Ms. Juncker stated that a Salmonella outbreak has been reported connected to jalapeños grown 
in Mexico.  
 
Ms. Juncker stated that measles cases are continuing to grow, but not in the state of 
Massachusetts. She stated that only two cases have been reported in Massachusetts.  
 
Ms. Juncker stated that they still have not seen Triple E cases in Massachusetts of either 
animal, human, or mosquito. She stated that they have not seen any animal or human cases of 
West Nile virus but mosquito samples have increased. 
 
Ms. Juncker stated that there is a new tick-borne virus that was seen in New York called 
Bourbon virus. She stated that they will probably see it around Massachusetts in a couple of 
years. She stated that there is no commercially available test to test for this so doctors are 
having a difficulty identifying it. 
 
Ms. Juncker stated that she sent out letters and emails regarding the water quality report to the 
VP of Lahey, and the Associate Chief Medical Officer and VP for Medical Affairs at Mass 
General Brigham. She stated that she gave them information regarding the law, Gloucester’s 
sodium levels, what it means to the patients with sodium restrictions, and a link to facts on 
sodium and drinking water and resources for patients.
Page 6 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
August 6, 2026 
 
 
 
 
Regulatory Reporting 
 
 
Ms. Hurley reported on the implementation of a new ticketing system called Spiceworks to 
replace C-Click Fix for tracking Department work, which will help with volumetrics and workload 
management. She thanked the IT Department for their help with the software implementation. 
The Board discussed concerns about the efficiency of maintaining two separate systems and 
the burden of preparing monthly reports. Ms. Hurley stated that while the reporting does require 
significant effort, they are working to automate some processes to reduce the burden on staff. 
 
Ms. Hurley reported that Ms. Turko is working really hard right now to be as responsive as 
possible. She stated that she's proactively reaching out to property owners every week. 
 
Ms. Hurley reported that they have had some common food violations. She stated that Ms. 
Vorias is doing some terrific work right now and her newsletters have a 51% open rate. She 
stated that the courtesy walkthroughs are very effective. 
 
Concerns of the Board 
 
Next Regular Monthly Meeting Board of Health- The next regular Board of Health meeting is 
scheduled for Thursday, September 3, 2026 at 5:30 pm.
